title: Discovery - NorthBridge Capital / Redwood Inference
summary: Prospect exploring LLM summarization + analyst copilots. Main blocker is data residency / sovereignty requirements for EU clients and whether Redwood can guarantee processing stays in-region.
next_steps: Redwood to confirm EU region availability for hosted and Dedicated
Schedule technical deep dive on VPC/private options
transcript:
Meeting: Discovery - NorthBridge Capital / Redwood Inference
Date: 2025-02-04
Duration: 41 min

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Cool, thanks for making time. Quick intros?
[00:06] Megan (NorthBridge): Megan, I run our data platform team.
[00:10] Tom (NorthBridge): Tom, security. I jump in when we talk about residency and controls.
[00:15] Aisha (Redwood): Aisha, solutions engineer.

[01:02] Alex: What are you trying to ship first?
[01:06] Megan: Internal research assistant. We do a lot of doc summarization and Q&A over PDFs, earnings calls, internal notes.
[01:20] Alex: Got it. And today are you using OpenAI or open models?
[01:25] Megan: Azure OpenAI for some teams, but we want an option that can do EU-only processing for some client work.

[02:10] Tom: Yeah, to be clear: we have clients where the data must stay in the EU. Not like “best effort,” like contractually.
[02:24] Alex: Understood. So data residency is a hard requirement for that segment.
[02:30] Tom: Correct. Some deals specify Frankfurt or “EU region” explicitly.

[04:05] Aisha: Redwood has hosted regions and we also do Dedicated pools. If you need a hard pin, Dedicated in an EU region is usually the cleanest.
[04:22] Megan: Is that still your control plane in the US?
[04:26] Aisha: Depends. For Private, we can run a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC. For hosted/dedicated, metadata is limited but we can walk through what is stored and where.

[06:10] Tom: The big thing for me is: the prompt and the outputs can’t transit out of region. Logs too, ideally.
[06:25] Alex: Okay. We’ll document what’s retained and how we can configure retention.

[10:42] Megan: Also latency. We’re fine with like 800ms to first token as long as throughput is stable.
[10:55] Aisha: That’s in the right range. We can show perf by model size and context length.

[18:30] Tom: Do you support EU-only audit log retention? Like if audit logs are generated, they also need to be stored in the EU.
[18:43] Aisha: For Private, yes — it’s your storage. For hosted, we have region-scoped logging, but we should confirm specifics for your policy.

[33:10] Alex: Recap: you want to test a pilot with an EU-only constraint, and we’ll confirm what’s possible in hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[33:24] Megan: Yes. If you can guarantee EU processing, we can move quickly.

[40:20] Alex: I’ll email next steps + set up the deep dive.
